C nearest block is pulled as far back as possible, it is deleted, and
C a 5-glider salvo is sent toward the other block; the salvo
C duplicates the block, creating a new one 10 units farther away and
C Deleting the eater on the western edge of the pattern gives
C population asymptotic to  C2 t^(2/3),  where  C2 = (45/256)^(1/3).

sawtooth6.name: sawtooth6
comments: CThis is an updated version of a sawtooth pattern originally
Cbuilt by David Bell on 29 Aug 1992.
CThere are two phases in the sawtooth's operation.
CIn the first phase, a stream of gliders travels to the receding
CCordership and are reflected back.  The density of the returning
Cstream is 1/2 that of the outgoing stream.  The population is at
Cthe new maximum at about the time that the first glider in the
Cstream returns so that the streams are full.
CIn the second phase, each returning glider impacts into an
Coutgoing glider to create an eater, which deletes the following
Coutput glider. This cuts off the output stream, which then
Cempties until there are no more gliders left.  The population is
Cat its minimum (again) at around the time that the last glider in
Cthe stream is used up so that the streams are empty.

jslife-oversize-20100113_linecrosser.name: jslife-oversize-20100113_linecrosser
comments: C A period 44160 diagonal line crossing mechanism.
C This demonstrates how a glider is able to get from one side of a diagonal
C line to the other side without destroying the line.  In doing this, the
C line is broken and stabilized, a glider is sent through the gap, and then
C the gap is healed.  This object uses many one-shot period 44160 glider
C guns having the proper synchronization.  The input glider comes from the
C lower left and is duplicated many times in order to enable all of the guns.
C The final glider emerges at the upper right.  The reaction can be repeated
C using input gliders at any multiple of 44160 generations.  Note: This is a
C highly unoptimized version of a line crosser, and can easily be improved.

ruler.name: ruler
comments: This produces groups of LWSSs headed west, with gaps of fixed size
between them.  The lengths of the groups form the 'ruler' sequence,
group of length n is emitted about generation 96*2^n.

a p48 glider gun by Noam Elkies (Jun 1997), a p8 glider reflector by
Noam Elkies (Sep 1998), and a p24 LWSS puffer (source unknown).

var-378+588n.name: var-378+588n
comments: C This is the first in a series of c/2 puffers having periods which
C are not a multiple of 4.  A phase-changing blinker puffer and a set
C of period 42 rakes creates a row of blinkers.
C Gliders from two more period 42 rakes ignite the blinker row, which
C burns faster than c/2 until it reaches a pair of period 6 ships.
C The next puffer in the series can be created by advancing all of the
C puffer except the rear rakes and their gliders by 168 generations.
C Then the resulting puffer has its period increased by 588 generations.
C The series thus contains periods 378, 966, 1554, and so on.
C Only 1/7 of the possible non-multiple of 4 periods using period 42
C rakes are covered by the series.  Adjusting the back rakes to ignite
C the blinker row in other ways may provide further coverage.
C This is a smaller version of a similar puffer built in March 2002.

p114blinker-2.name: p114blinker-2
comments: C A period 114 c/3 blinker puffer.
C This is based on an old dirty c/3 period 222 puffer engine.  Adding an
C evolving traffic lights behind the exhaust converts the puffer into a
C period 114 blinker puffer since the perturbation is self-sustaining.
C The output can be perturbed using period 3 ships to create clean rakes.

p114forwrake-1.name: p114forwrake-1
comments: C A period 114 c/3 forward rake.
C This uses a period 114 puffer engine by Jason Summers whose output is
C modified by edge-spark spaceships to produce a clean rake.

p114forwrake-2.name: p114forwrake-2
comments: C A period 114 c/3 forward rake.
C This uses a period 114 puffer engine by Jason Summers whose output is
C modified by edge-spark spaceships to produce a clean rake.

p114forwrake-3.name: p114forwrake-3
comments: C A period 114 c/3 forward rake.
C This is the first clean rake found for the period 114 engine.
C This uses two period 114 blinker puffers whose output is perturbed
C to create gliders which delete the blinkers and release another glider.

p114pulsar.name: p114pulsar
comments: C A c/3 period 114 pulsar puffer.
C This is based on an impact from two period 114 glider streams.
C The streams impact into a period 21 frothing spaceship but the
C impacts modify the froth's period to be compatible with the

p114smoke.name: p114smoke
comments: C A period 114 c/3 ship which generates a smoke cloud.
C This is based on a period 114 blinker puffer found by Jason Summers
C on a frothing puffer engine found by Paul Tooke whose output is
C perturbed by edge-spark spaceships so as to leave only a cloud of
C smoke.  The cloud can be used to perturb gliders to produce a
C variety of output.  This is a much smaller version of an original

p1260forwrake.name: p1260forwrake
comments: C A period 1260 c/3 forward rake.
C This uses two period 180 rakes whose output is period multiplied by 7
C by a period 21 frothing spaceship.

p129.name: p129
comments: C A period 129 c/3 dirty puffer.
C The period is 43*3, and results from a perturbation of a frothing
C puffer engine found by Paul Tooke.  This could be turned into a
C clean period 129 rake (with a lot of work) by using a perturbation
C to liberate a foward glider, and then using glider duplicating and
C turning reactions to delete all of the output.

p129forwrake.name: p129forwrake
comments: C A period 129 c/3 forward rake.
C This is based on a perturbation of a frothing spaceship found by
C Paul Tooke.  The perturbation results in a period 129 dirty puffer.
C Adding further period 3 spaceships liberates a forward glider,
C which is fed into four glider duplication convoys to create extra
C gliders to clean up all of the puffer's output.

p135forwrake-1.name: p135forwrake-1
comments: C This uses a period 45 puffer whose output is perturbed to become a
C period 135 puffer, and two period 45 forwards rakes which interact
C with the output to allow one glider through.  This is an improved

p135forwrake-2.name: p135forwrake-2
comments: C This uses a period 45 puffer whose output is perturbed to become a
C period 135 puffer, and two period 45 forwards rakes which interact
C with the output to allow one glider through.

p144forwrake.name: p144forwrake
comments: C A period 144 c/3 forward rake.
C This uses two period 72 forward rakes whose output hits a period 21
C frothing spaceship.  The period of the spaceship is modified by the
C impacts to be compatible with the glider streams.

p15-1.name: p15-1
comments: C Period 15 c/3 spaceship with its engine at one side.
C This spaceship allows maximum access to the engine's output by a glider
C coming from one side.  In particular, a backwards travelling glider can
C be perturbed by the exhaust so as to become a boat.

p15-2.name: p15-2
comments: C A period 15 c/3 spaceship which has one side shorter than the other and
C bent far upwards.  All the reactions using a forwards glider or sideways
C standard spaceship which clears the engine at the back are possible
C since the short arm is not in the way.

p15-5.name: p15-5
comments: C A period 15 c/3 spaceship with sparks at the back.
C This was the first period 15 spaceship found.  This ship has very wide
C arms which prevent gliders from reaching the sparks.  Later versions of
C this ship have better arms which do allow gliders to reach the sparks.

p15beehive.name: p15beehive
comments: C A period 15 c/3 beehive puffer.
C The beehives are close enough together to be ignited and can burn

p15dup.name: p15dup
comments: C A period 45 c/3 spaceship which can duplicate a forward glider into
C another forward glider and a backward glider.

p15turners.name: p15turners
comments: C Three glider turning reactions for period 15 c/3 spaceships.
C These use period 15 spaceships to turn forwards gliders into the other

p162forwrake.name: p162forwrake
comments: C A period 162 c/3 forward rake.
C This uses a period 81 foward rake whose output is thinned using a

p18-1.name: p18-1
comments: C A c/3 period 18 puffer which leaves pairs of boats.

p18-2.name: p18-2
comments: C This is a period 18 c/3 puffer which produces two boats in each period.

p180backrake-1.name: p180backrake-1
comments: C A c/3 period 180 backward rake.
C This uses a period 180 forward rake whose gliders are turned using
C a period 15 spaceship.  The p15 spaceship can be moved inwards if
C the block deleting spaceships are also moved downwards.

p180backrake-2.name: p180backrake-2
comments: C A c/3 period 180 backwards rake.
C This works by using two period 90 backwards rakes to perturb the back of a
C period 24 spaceship, to form a period 180 clean spaceship.  Gliders from
C another period 90 spaceship then pass by the back of the spaceship, and
C every other glider is deleted by the back sparks.  This forwards rake is
C then converted to a backwards rake by a period 15 spaceship.

p180block.name: p180block
comments: C A period 180 c/3 block puffer.
C This uses a period 90 forward rake whose gliders impact into a period 21
C frothing spaceship to create the block.

p180forwmwss-1.name: p180forwmwss-1
comments: C A c/3 period 180 forward MWSS rake.
C This shoots a MWSS stream which travels forwards ahead of the puffer.
C The MWSS's are created using a normal three glider collision, where the
C gliders are produced by a period 180 backwards rake and two period 45
C forward rakes.  This is a much improved version of an older rake.

p180forwmwss-2.name: p180forwmwss-2
comments: C A c/3 period 180 forwards MWSS rake.
C This shoots a MWSS stream which travels forwards ahead of the puffer.
C The MWSS's are created using a normal three glider collision, where the
C gliders are produced by a period 180 backwards rake and two period 180
C forward rakes.  A final period 90 rake and period 3 spaceship is required
C to clean up the debris when only two of the gliders collide.

p180forwrake-1.name: p180forwrake-1
comments: C A c/3 period 180 forward rake.
C This is produced by a one-sided impact of a period 90 glider stream into
C a period 21 frothing spaceship.  The period of the spaceship is modified
C by the impacts to be compatible with the glider stream.  Period 180
C c/3 rakes were previously known, but this one is much smaller.

p180forwrake-2.name: p180forwrake-2
comments: C A c/3 period 180 forwards rake.
C This works by using two period 90 backwards rakes to perturb the back of a
C period 24 spaceship, to form a period 180 clean spaceship.  Gliders from
C another period 90 spaceship then pass by the back of the spaceship, and
C every other glider is deleted by the back sparks.  This is an improved
C version of an earlier rake.

p180thing.name: p180thing
comments: C A c/3 period 180 puffer which produces a large still life.
C This uses two period 90 rakes whose gliders impact into a period 21
C frothing spaceship.  The period of the spaceship is modified by the
C impacts to be compatible with the incoming glider streams.

p21-1.name: p21-1
comments: C This is a smaller version of the original period 21 c/3 spaceship.

p21-2.name: p21-2
comments: C The engine was found from a truncated spaceship search, and was the
C first success of such a search other than period 2 spaceships.

p216forwrake.name: p216forwrake
comments: C A c/3 period 216 forward rake.
C The gliders are produced by a period tripling reaction on a pair of
C period 72 glider streams.  The tripling reaction uses a period 21
C frothing spaceship whose period is modified by the impacts to be
C compatible with the glider streams.

p222-1.name: p222-1
comments: C A dirty period 222 c/3 puffer.
C This produces the same output as a previously known period 222 puffer,

p222-2.name: p222-2
comments: C After stabilization, this puffer produces some junk every 222 generations.
C Part of the junk is a pulsar.  The front of the puffer is a period 9 ship.

p225forwrake-1.name: p225forwrake-1
comments: C A c/3 period 225 forwards rake.
C This uses five period 45 forwards rakes and a period 24 spaceship.
C The impacts of the gliders changes the period of the p24 spaceship
C to be a multiple of 45.  This is an improved version of this rake.

p225forwrake-2.name: p225forwrake-2
comments: C A c/3 period 225 forwards rake.
C This uses five period 45 forwards rakes and a period 24 spaceship,

p225forwrake-3.name: p225forwrake-3
comments: C A c/3 period 225 forward rake.
C This is produced by a period quintupling reaction on two period 45
C glider streams.  The period multiplying reaction uses a period 21
C frothing spaceship whose period is modified by the impacts to be
C compatible with the glider streams.

p228forwrake.name: p228forwrake
comments: C A c/3 period 228 forward rake.
C This is produced by period doubling of two period 114 input streams.
C The period doubling reaction uses a period 21 frothing spaceship whose
C period is modified by the impacts to be compatible with the glider streams.

p24block.name: p24block
comments: C A period 24 c/3 puffer which produces a block every period.  It was formed
C by perturbing the exhaust of a period 54 c/3 puffer such that the perturbation

p24turner.name: p24turner
comments: C A glider turning reaction using a period 24 c/3 spaceship.
C A forward glider is turned into a reversed forwards glider.

p270forwrake-1.name: p270forwrake-1
comments: C A period 270 c/3 forwards rake.
C This uses two period 90 rakes, a period 24 ship, and two period 3 ships.
C This is am improvement of a previous version of this rake.

p270forwrake-2.name: p270forwrake-2
comments: C A period 270 c/3 forwards rake.
C This uses two period 90 rakes, a period 24 ship, and two period 3 ships.

p27backrake.name: p27backrake
comments: C A period 27 c/3 backward rake.
C This is created by a perturbation of a c/3 frothing puffer.
C Stephen Silver replaced one of the original perturbing spaceships
C of the rake with the smaller perturbing spaceship shown here.

p27blockstoglider.name: p27blockstoglider
comments: C A period 27 c/3 convoy which converts blocks into backward gliders.
C This uses two period 27 smoking spaceships.  Forward gliders can
C easily be turned into blocks using small period 3 spaceships.
C This reaction allows the blocks can be restored to gliders at a

p27dup.name: p27dup
comments: C A period 27 c/3 glider duplication convoy.
C This converts a backward glider into a forward glider and another
C backward glider, both traveling back through the same columns.
C This uses period 27 c/3 smoking ships found by Paul Tooke.

p27forwrake-1.name: p27forwrake-1
comments: C A period 27 c/3 forward rake.
C This uses a period 27 backward rake whose gliders impact into the smoke
C of a period 27 ship to create forward gliders.  The backward rake and
C smoking ship were found by Paul Tooke.

p27forwrake-2.name: p27forwrake-2
comments: C A period 27 c/3 forward rake.
C This uses two period 27 c/3 backward rakes whose gliders react in
C a kickback reaction.  The backward rakes were found by Paul Tooke.

p27sidelwss.name: p27sidelwss
comments: C A period 27 c/3 sideways LWSS rake.
C This uses two period 27 backward rakes and a period 27 block puffer.

p27sidemwss.name: p27sidemwss
comments: C A period 27 c/3 sideways MWSS rake.
C This uses a period 27 backward rake, a period 27 block puffer,
C and a period 27 smoking ship.

p27smoke.name: p27smoke
comments: C A period 27 c/3 smoking spaceship.
C The smoke from this ship sticks out three cells from the edge of the
C main ship, and so can be used to perturb other objects as it passes by.
C In addition, the smoke can be further perturbed to produce many

p27thing.name: p27thing
comments: C This produces 12-bit still life which has an eater component.

p27toad.name: p27toad
comments: C A period 27 c/3 toad puffer.
C This uses the impact of a period 27 backward rake into the smoke

p27turners.name: p27turners
comments: C Glider turning reactions for gliders produced by period 27 c/3 rakes.
C This use a period 27 c/3 smoking spaceship found by Paul Tooke.

p315forwrake.name: p315forwrake
comments: C A c/3 period 315 forward rake.
C In this rake one glider out of every 7 from a single period 45 glider
C stream is perturbed by a period 21 frothing ship with no change of the
C froth's behavior.  This same reaction can be used to multiply the period
C of any c/3 rake by 7 if it doesn't already have that factor in its period.

p333forwrake.name: p333forwrake
comments: C Engineless c/3 p333 forward rake.
C The same basic design can also build any c/3 forward rake which
C has a period of the form 333 + 6N.
C Assembled by Jason Summers, from components by David Bell

p342forwrake.name: p342forwrake
comments: C A c/3 period 342 forward rake.
C This uses a period tripling reaction on period 114 glider streams.
C The tripling uses a period 21 frothing spaceship whose period is
C modified by the impacts to be compatible with the glider streams.

p36.name: p36
comments: C This leaves four blocks each period.  The back of the puffer consists
C of two different period 3 c/3 spaceships which perturb the engine's
C exhaust.  (The engine self-destructs without the perturbations.)
C Either of the back spaceships can be removed and replaced with a
C symmetrical copy of the remaining spaceship to form a different puffer.

p360forwrake.name: p360forwrake
comments: C A c/3 period 360 forward rake.
C This is produced by a period doubling reaction on period 180 input streams.
C The period doubling uses a period 21 frothing spaceship whose period is
C modified by the impacts to be compatible with the glider streams.

p36backrake-1.name: p36backrake-1
comments: C A c/3 period 36 backward rake.
C This is built from two slightly dirty backward c/3 rakes whose
C gliders clean each other up.  This is an improved version of this rake.

p36backrake-2.name: p36backrake-2
comments: C A c/3 period 36 backward rake.
C This is built from two slightly dirty backward c/3 rakes whose
C gliders clean each other up.

p3bigsmoke.name: p3bigsmoke
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a glider into a big cloud of smoke.
C The smoke reaches out 15 cells beyond the edge of the convoy and so
C can be used to perturb many objects as the convoy passes by.

p3dup-1.name: p3dup-1
comments: C A period 3 c/3 forward glider duplicator.
C This is a convoy of period 3 ships which converts an incoming
C forward glider to two outgoing forward gliders.  The two gliders
C travel in opposite sideways directions.  The minimum repeat time
C of the reaction is 63 generations.

p3dup-2.name: p3dup-2
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which duplicates a forward glider.
C Both output gliders continue in the original direction.

p3dup-3.name: p3dup-3
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which duplicates a forward glider.
C This produces a forward and a backward output glider which travel
C back through the same columns as the incoming glider.

p3dup-4.name: p3dup-4
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which duplicates a foward glider.
C There is one forward and one backward output glider which travel
C back through the same columns as the incoming glider.
C This is an improved version of a previous version of this convoy.

p3dup-5.name: p3dup-5
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which duplicates a forward glider.
C This produces two backward gliders which travel in opposite sideways
C directions.  This is a smaller version of an earlier reaction.

p3dup-6.name: p3dup-6
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which duplicates a foward glider.
C This produces one forward and one backward glider which travel in
C the same sideways direction as the incoming glider.
C This is an improvement on a previous version of this convoy.

p3glidertoblock-1.name: p3glidertoblock-1
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a forward glider into a block.
C The block is situated so that there is a clear path forwards through
C the convoy, so that if the block is transformed into a LWSS using two
C impacting gliders, the LWSS could escape forwards.

p3glidertoblock-2.name: p3glidertoblock-2
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a forward glider into a block.
C The block is situated so that there is a clear path forwards through
C the convoy, so that if the block is transformed into a LWSS using two
C impacting gliders, the LWSS could escape forwards.  This is an improved
C version of a previous version of this convoy.

p3glidertolwss-1.name: p3glidertolwss-1
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which converts a forward glider into a backward LWSS.
C Removing one of the spaceships at the back allows a glider to escape so
C this can also act as a glider duplicator.  This is an improved version of
C a previous version of this convoy.

p3glidertolwss-2.name: p3glidertolwss-2
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which converts a forward glider into a backward LWSS.
C Removing one of the spaceships at the back allows a glider to escape so
C this can also act as a glider duplicator.

p3glidertolwss-3.name: p3glidertolwss-3
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which converts a forward glider into a backward LWSS.
C The glider is first converted into another glider and block.  The glider
C is duplicated into a pair of gliders.  One of the gliders is turned into
C a backward LWSS and an unwanted loaf.  The other glider impacts the block
C to produce a honey farm which is then perturbed into a glider which

p3honeyfarms.name: p3honeyfarms
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which can turn a forward glider into a honey
C farm, and then also turn the evolving honey farm into a series of new
C honey farms each of which is shifted upwards by 5 cells and sideways by
C 6 cells.  The final honey farm can then be perturbed into output gliders.
C This is an improvement of a previoys convoy.

p3lwssreflect-1.name: p3lwssreflect-1
comments: C A pair of period 3 c/3 convoys which reflect a pair of LWSSs back
C and forth between them as they recede from each other.  This is an
C improvement of a previous version of this object.

p3lwssreflect-2.name: p3lwssreflect-2
comments: C A pair of period 3 c/3 convoys which reflect a pair of LWSSs back and
C forth between them as they recede from each other.

p3lwsstoglider-1.name: p3lwsstoglider-1
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which converts a forward LWSS into a forward glider.

p3lwsstoglider-2.name: p3lwsstoglider-2
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which converts a forward LWSS to a backward glider.
C This is an improved version of this convoy.

p3lwsstoglider-3.name: p3lwsstoglider-3
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which converts a backward LWSS to a forward glider.
C The LWSS is first turned into a traffic lights, which is perturbed into
C a honey farm, which then produces the forward glider.  There are variations
C of the final reaction to produce other output.  This is an improved version

p3lwsstoglider-4.name: p3lwsstoglider-4
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which converts a forward LWSS to a forward glider.
C This has a repeat time of 96 or larger.

p3mwsstoglider.name: p3mwsstoglider
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which converts a forward MWSS into a backward glider.
C This is an improved version of this convoy.

p3notmonotonic.name: p3notmonotonic
comments: C A period 3 c/3 spaceship whose leading edge is not monotonic.
C That is, its leading edge falls back in one of its generations.

p3shift-1.name: p3shift-1
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which shifts a forward glider.
C This is an improved version of a previous version of this convoy.

p3shift-2.name: p3shift-2
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which shifts the path of a forward glider.
C This uses a glider to honey farm conversion.  The evolving honey
C farm is then turned into another honey farm.  The final honey farm
C is perturbed into the output glider.  Adding more honey farm stages
C or changing the final honey farm conversion reaction can produce
C output gliders on other paths.  This is an improved version of this

p3sidetagalong.name: p3sidetagalong
comments: C This shows a small period 3 tagalong component which needs a
C single spark to maintain it.

p3symdup.name: p3symdup
comments: C A period 3 c/3 symmetrical glider duplicator.
C This creates two forward gliders from one input glider such that
C the two output gliders travel on symmetrical paths.  The gliders
C can be used to impact into the two sides of a symmetrical c/3
C spaceship or other object to perturb them.  This is an improved

p3turn-1.name: p3turn-1
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a foward glider into a backward glider.
C The output glider continues in the same sideways direction.
C This is an improved version of this convoy.

p3turn-2.name: p3turn-2
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a foward glider into a forward glider.
C The output glider travels back through the same columns.
C This is an improvement of a previous version of this reaction.

p3turn-3.name: p3turn-3
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a foward glider into a backward glider.
C The output glider travels back through the same columns.
C This is an improvement on a previous version of this convoy.

p3turn-4.name: p3turn-4
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a foward glider into a backward glider.
C The output glider travels back through the same columns.
C This is an improvement of a previous version of this convoy.

p3turn-5.name: p3turn-5
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a foward glider into a backward glider.
C The output glider travels back through the same columns.
C This is an improvement of a previous version of this convoy.

p3turn-6.name: p3turn-6
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a foward glider into a forward glider.
C The output glider travels back through the same columns.

p3turn-7.name: p3turn-7
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a foward glider into a forward glider.
C The output glider travels back through the same columns.
C This is an improvment on a previous version of this convoy.

p3turn-8.name: p3turn-8
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a foward glider into a forward glider.
C The output glider travels back through the same columns.
C This is an improved version of a previous version of this convoy.

p3turn-9.name: p3turn-9
comments: C A period 3 c/3 convoy which turns a forward glider.
C The glider travels back through the same columns.  This is based on a
C period 3 glider duplicator which has one of its gliders deleted.

p3w14l20.name: p3w14l20
comments: C The period 3 c/3 ships which fit in an area of width 14 and length 20.
C The first one shown is the turtle, found by Dean Hickerson.  The one
C at the end was found by Tim Coe.  The rest are by Stephen Silver.

p405backrake-1.name: p405backrake-1
comments: C This uses two period 45 c/3 forward rakes whose gliders impact into
C the back of a period 24 c/3 ship to produce occasional debris.
C The debris is perturbed and a final period 45 c/3 rake is used to
C produce the output gliders.  The phase of the period 24 ship is
C changed by the glider impacts to allow the odd period to occur.
C This is an improvement of a previous version of this rake.

p405backrake-2.name: p405backrake-2
comments: C This uses two period 45 c/3 forward rakes whose gliders impact into
C the back of a period 24 c/3 ship to produce occasional debris.
C The debris is perturbed and a final period 45 c/3 rake is used to
C produce the output gliders.  The phase of the period 24 ship is
C changed by the glider impacts to allow the odd period to occur.

p45-1.name: p45-1
comments: C A period 45 c/3 puffer which produces four blocks every period.
C This is a smaller version of the original period 45 puffer.

p45-2.name: p45-2
comments: C A period 45 c/3 puffer which produces four blocks every period.
C This was the first puffer found which has an odd period.  The exhaust
C of this puffer can easily be perturbed by c/3 edge spark spaceships to
C produce much dirtier puffers, or to produce clean rakes.

p45.name: p45
comments: C A period 45 c/3 spaceship created from a period 45 c/3 puffer along with
C two c/3 edge spark spaceships which manage to destroy the exhaust.

p456forwrake.name: p456forwrake
comments: C A c/3 period 456 forward rake.
C This is produced by the period quadrupling of two period 114 input streams.
C This uses a period multiplication reaction based on a period 21 frothing
C spaceship.  The period of the spaceship is modified by the impacts to be
C compatible with the glider streams.  The frothing spaceship shows three

p45backmwss.name: p45backmwss
comments: C A c/3 period 45 backwards MWSS rake.
C This produces a backwards travelling MWSS every 45 generations.
C It is composed of a period 45 spaceship which produces a cloud of smoke
C every 45 generations, a period 3 edge-spark spaceship which perturbs the
C smoke into pre-blocks, and a period 45 forwards rake, whose gliders impact
C on the pre-blocks to form the MWSS's.

p45backrake-1.name: p45backrake-1
comments: C This uses a period 45 base puffer whose output is perturbed by one large
C period 3 edge spark spaceship and five small period 3 spaceships into a
C backwards glider.  This is an improvement on previous versions of this

p45backrake-2.name: p45backrake-2
comments: C A period 45 c/3 backward rake.

p45backrake-3.name: p45backrake-3
comments: C This uses a period 45 base puffer whose output is perturbed by three
C period 3 c/3 edge-spark spaceships into a backwards glider.

p45backrake-4.name: p45backrake-4
comments: C This uses a period 45 base puffer whose output is perturbed by five
C period 3 c/3 edge-spark spaceships into a backwards glider.

p45backrake-5.name: p45backrake-5
comments: C This uses a period 45 base puffer whose output is perturbed by three
C period 3 c/3 edge-spark spaceships into two backwards gliders.
C The backmost edge c/3 edge spark spaceship deletes one of the gliders.

p45blinker.name: p45blinker
comments: C A period 45 c/3 puffer which produces just a blinker every period.

p45block-1.name: p45block-1
comments: C A period 45 c/3 puffer which produces a block every period.

p45block-2.name: p45block-2

p495-1.name: p495-1
comments: C This is a period 495 c/3 spaceship.
C This is the first in a series of spaceships with odd periods.
C This works using several period 45 rakes and a loop of LWSS's and boats.
C All periods of the form 45 * (3N + 1) or 45 * (3N + 2) can be
C obtained by modification as described below.
C In this spaceship, there are two LWSS's (or boats) traveling in the loop
C at any time.  Removing one of them produces the "base" spaceship having
C the period 990.  This base period is the important number used to calculate
C and construct the next spaceship in the series.
C To create the next spaceship in the series, you need to do the following
C painful steps.  Delete all LWSS's and boats except for the single LWSS
C directly behind the top period 45 c/3 spaceship.  Move that front c/3
C spaceship and it's LWSS upwards by 30 cells.  Doing this will increase
C the period of the base spaceship by 270 generations.  In this example,
C the new period will become 990+270 = 1260.  Then divide out all factors
C of two from the period.  Here, this becomes 1260/4 = 315.  This period
C will become the period of the next spaceship in the series, and the number
C of LWSS's and boats in that ship will be the quotient, in this case 4.
C Now to actually create the new spaceship, remember the position of the
C original LWSS, and run the new base spaceship the number of generations
C indicated for the next odd period spaceship (e.g., 315).  Insert another
C LWSS behind the front c/3 spaceship in the same position as the original
C LWSS.  Continue running and inserting until the loop is fully populated.
C You may also have to run a few more cycles in order to make the "tail" of
C blinkers and loafs stabilize.  Then you have the new odd period spaceship.
C Note that for the first two adjustments, the top period 45 backwards rakes
C have to be moved outwards to make room for the moved period 45 ship.
C This is a snaller version of a previous period 495 spaceship.

C This rake has an engine convoy at the front, two convoys
C  forming lines behind that, and a V-shaped convoy at the back.
C  The recipe to create the next rake in the series is:
C   - Move the top line convoy orthogonally right by 6 cells.
C   - Move the left line convoy orthogonally down by 6 cells.
C   - Move the V-shaped convoy diagonally back by 6 cells.
C  This will increase the period by 32 generations.
C The modifications can be be made in the opposite direction
C  to form the earlier rakes in the series. Moving the convoys
C  by 300 cells creates the first rake in the series (period 4508).
C Note that each rake has to be run a few cycles before it becomes
C  fully populated and begins to emit gliders.
C David Bell with Jason Summers and Nicolay Beluchenko, 13 Oct 2005

rand-1.name: rand-1
comments: C A c/3 rake that produces a stream of gliders determined by a pseudo-random
C number generator.  Many gliders already output by the device are shown
C in the pattern.  This is a smaller version of a previous pattern.
C The base period is 90 generations, and gliders are (possibly) emitted at
C multiples of this base period.  The output is generated based on the
C pattern of the absence or presence of MWSS's and blinkers within the device.
C These (possibly present) MWSS's and blinkers form a loop within the device.
C MWSS's head upwards to the front of the device, and are turned into blinkers
C which remain until the middle of the device catches up to them.  The blinkers
C are then used to XOR the MWSS's stream to change its state.  The stream of
C MWSS's is detected at the top of the device to produce the output gliders.
C Moving the period 45 spaceship at the head of the MWSS stream upwards by
C multiples of 30 cells increases the number of bits in the PRNG, which can
C increase the period of the device.  This is based on a design for a moving
C PRNG by Dean Hickerson, with some modifications of my own.

s9-1.name: s9-1
comments: C This is a "moving" sawtooth pattern constructed of two period 90 c/3 rakes,
C a period 8 c/2 blinker puffer, and three period 3 edge-repair spaceships.
C This sawtooth has an expansion factor of three.  This sawtooth is an
C improvement on a previous one.
C The blinker puffer lays down a trail of blinkers.  Meanwhile the two c/3
C rakes produce pairs of backwards gliders which normally destroy each other.
C But eventually a pair of the gliders hits the end of the trail of blinkers.
C This ignites the blinker trail and creates a block and a glider.  The block
C and glider are deleted by period 3 edge-repair spaceships.  The blinker
C trail burns up completely, completing the cycle.  But in each cycle, the
C c/2 blinker puffer moves further ahead of the c/3 rakes, so the blinker
C trail becomes longer in a geometric progression.
C Removing the single or the pair of edge-repair spaceships at the back
C results in a pattern which grows in a logarithmic manner where a glider
C of block is emitted at increasing intervals.

fermatprimes.name: fermatprimes
comments: C This is a Fermat prime calculator, rigged to self-destruct and stop
C growing if any Fermat primes over 65537 turn up. Since the
C existence of such primes is an unsolved problem in mathematics,
C it is unknown if this pattern grows to infinite population.
C The tubs in a row represent the known Fermat primes, starting
C with 5. The other three represent 17, 257, and 65537. A tub gets
C destroyed whenever a Fermat prime is found. In the unlikely event
C that an additional Fermat prime exists, the pond will eventually be
C destroyed, followed by the puffers and breeders.
C A number N is tested at about generation 120N - 550, so the tubs
C will be destroyed at about generations: 50; 1,490; 30,290; and
C The next-smallest Fermat number that is not known to be composite
C is 2^2^31+1. Therefore, the pond (and the breeders) will survive at
C least 10^640,000,000 generations. So don't expect to see anything
C interesting happen by watching this pattern. Remove the tubs if you
C want to see the destruction.
C The careful observer may notice that actually every number of the
C form 2^N+1 is tested for primality, while Fermat numbers are of the
C form 2^(2^N)+1. However, numbers of the form M^N+1 can never be
C prime unless N is a power of 2, so the only primes of the form 2^N+1
C are in fact the Fermat primes.
C The "Primer" and "Caber Tosser" patterns used here are by Dean
C Hickerson. The beehive puffer is by Hartmut Holzwart.

DOPPLER.name: DOPPLER
comments: CThis p48 double glider rake visualizes a basic wave physics effect in Life. I named
Cit after the Austrian physicist Christian Doppler (1803 - 1853) for two reasons:
C- The double glider rake demonstrates the Doppler effect in the Life universe.
C- Doppler is also the German word for "doubler".
CDoppler discovered 1842 that the observed frequency of periodical waves is
Cchanged if the source of the waves moves with respect to the observer. Well
Cknown examples of this frequency shift are the acoustical and the optical Doppler
CEvery 48 generations the rake emits two gliders, one in the backward and one in
Cthe forward direction. Note the large distance of successive gliders in the
Cbackward stream and the much smaller distance of gliders in the forward stream.
CIn view of the fact that the Doppler rake emits equal numbers of gliders into both
Cstreams, these different distances appear to be counterintuitive.
CA Life astronomer would see the frequency of the backward gliders red-shifted
Cwhereas the forward stream's frequency would appear blue-shifted to him or her.
CFor applications of the Doppler rake see the patterns BREEDER1.LIF and

VERY_1ST.name: VERY_1ST
comments: CIn November of 1970 the first glider gun was discovered by Bill Gosper' group at
CMIT.This is a well known historic fact. But was the famous p30 glider gun really
Cthe first gun to be discovered?  William Poundstone writes in his book "The
CRecursive Universe" (Contemporary Books, Inc., Chicago, 1985, ISBN
CThe shuttle is provocative - it tries to produce a beehive every fifteen
Cgenerations. This seems so close to unlimited growth. If the old beehives moved
Cout of the way, it would be. A group of MIT students including R. William Gosper,
CJr., Robert April, Michael Beeler, Richard Howell, Rich Schroeppel, and Michael
CSpeciner wondered if there was some way to modify the shuttle to produce gliders
Cinstead. They tried to arrange two shuttles to interact periodically. There are many
Cways that two shuttles can interact. They can meet at 90 degrees or at 180
Cdegrees. They can be in phase or out of phase by any number of generations up
Cto twenty-nine. They can meet head on or a little off to the side. Gosper's group
Cexperimented on a computer and found an arrangement of shuttles that produces
Ca glider. Unfortunately, the glider crashed into one of the shuttles and destroyed it.
CAfter further experimentation, Gosper's group found a true glider gun.
CAha, there was another gun even before the famous first gun! Although it was
Cextremely short-lived (it shot itself to death with the very first glider it fired), it was a
Cgun nevertheless. Here is this very first glider gun. Luckily, there is a way to save
Cthe gun's life permanently by adding a third queen bee shuttle. The additional
Cshuttle has nothing to do with the glider production. It only deflects the gliders to
Canother path before they can crash into the gun.
CThe very first glider gun even comes in three different variants: The life-saving
Cthird shuttle can be delayed by four or eight generations and shifted by one or two
Ccells to SW with respect to the variant shown here.
CFor a use of the very first glider gun see the pattern GG15.LIF.
CBill Gosper et al, 1970 (refound and fixed by Dieter Leithner, before 1996)
